artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each i ≥ 1 let K_i ⊂ ℂ be a nonempty compact set containing 0, and assume that diam(K_i) → 0 as i → ∞ (so that every choice sequence (x_j) with x_j ∈ K_j produces an absolutely convergent series ∑ x_j). Define the achievement set
   S = { ∑_{j=1}^∞ x_j : x_j ∈ K_j for all j }
and, for each integer z ≥ 0, the tail achievement set
   R_z = { ∑_{i=z+1}^∞ x_i : x_i ∈ K_i for all i > z }.
Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the sequence (K_i) (equivalently, on the tails R_z) under which S = ℂ.
artifact.category_tag: Achievement sets of null sequences in ℂ
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on achievement sets in ℝ² and ℂ (e.g., works on perturbations of geometric/multigeometric series and achievement sets in R²) addresses related questions and provides examples, but no general necessary-and-sufficient condition characterizing when the achievement set of a complex null sequence equals all of ℂ has been published. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Achievement Sets of Series in R^2
status_evidence.snippet: We examine the properties of achievement sets of series in R^2... several examples of unusual sets of subsums on the plane.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies achievement sets in the plane but does not provide a complete characterization of when S = ℂ.

status_evidence.title: Achievement sets on the plane—Perturbations of geometric and multigeometric series
status_evidence.snippet: Considering the sets of subsums of series (or achievement sets) we show that for conditionally convergent series the multidimensional case is much more complicated than that of the real line.
status_evidence.claim: The planar/complex case is known to be substantially more intricate than the real case, and a general criterion for S = ℂ is not established.
